text:
B: Hiya, hello. Can you hear me alright?
A: Yes, hello, I can hear you. Sorry, my English is not perfect, so be patient with me, yeah?
B: Don't be daft, you sound fine. I'm Julie, I'm in Ossett, near Wakefield.
A: I'm Dorota, from Walsall. Well, from Poland originally, Bydgoszcz, but Walsall nearly twenty years.
B: Twenty years, you're a local now, then. So what do you do?
A: I'm pharmacy technician, in independent pharmacy in Bloxwich. Dispensing, checking, and the blister packs for care homes, you know? That's big part of my week.
B: Oh, that's a responsible job, that. You can't get them wrong.
A: No, no. My pharmacist trusts me on the bench, he says I'm very accurate. But the admin, erm, the CPD for my registration, I always do the week before deadline. Every time!
B: Ha, I'd be on your case about that. I'm a regional operations manager for a builders' merchants, six branches, so I'm forever chasing people for paperwork.
A: Six! I thought from your photo, she is very organised lady. I said it, honestly.
B: Well, I try. Twenty-four years I've been there, started as an admin clerk. So it can be done.
A: That's very good. Erm, sometimes I think about doing the accuracy checking course, for technicians. Bit more money. But I don't ask my boss, I just think about it.
B: Ask him. Honestly, ask him Monday. If you don't ask, they'll never offer, believe me. I've learnt that the hard way.
A: You're right. Monday. Maybe Tuesday, Monday is busy.
B: Tuesday, then, I'll let you off. Have you got family over here?
A: My son Kacper, he's seventeen, at college. And my daughter is in Birmingham. My mum and sister are in Poland still. My mum is eighty, so I worry, you know? I go every summer, but is far.
B: Oh, I know. My dad's in Wakefield, which is ten minutes, and I still don't go enough. My sister does most of it. I feel awful about it, to be honest.
A: Ten minutes is good though. You can just go, one evening, on the way back from work, yeah?
B: I know, I know. It's the M1, it's work, it's the dog. Excuses, really.
A: Is always something. I don't judge, I'm the same with church, I say I go every Sunday, then I'm knackered and I don't.
B: Ha, I'm Christmas and funerals, me. So you're Catholic, then? I saw the cross.
A: Yes. Polish Mass in Walsall. It helps, especially last few years.
B: That's nice. Each to their own, I always say. So what are you having for your tea tonight?
A: Honestly? Fish fingers in a bap. Nobody can be bothered in my house today.
B: A bap! You've gone West Midlands. Up here it's a bread cake.
A: Bread cake? That's a cake, not bread!
B: Don't start, that's a whole argument in Yorkshire. Tonight it's a chilli for us, Gary's out on a job till all hours so it'll be
